scope: All JAIR appendices and corresponding LNCS parts, including generated-table captions. Read-only manuscript review.

proposals.old: This appendix reports the full agent set for Tiger, Diagnosis, Bandit, and the two Tileworld grids, one table per environment.
proposals.new: This appendix reports the per-environment results for Tiger, Diagnosis, Bandit, and the two Tileworld grids, omitting the duplicate rows identified in Appendix~\ref{app:core_details}.
proposals.rationale: Avoids promising every agent row when the manuscript explicitly says the tables omit duplicate untuned Info Gain and Tiger pymdp-AIF rows. The later appendix already specifies exactly which rows are omitted.

proposals.old: Bold marks the best value in the success and reward columns, with exact ties bold together.
proposals.new: Bold marks the best value in the success and reward columns, with exact ties bolded together.
proposals.rationale: Repairs a grammatical omission without changing the bolding rule.

proposals.old: EFE and Planning are bit-identical at $K{=}1$ and within seed-level sampling error at $K{=}2$ ($43.2\%$ against $43.8\%$ success, the multi-test evidence at that scale being carried by the main Diagnosis battery of Section~\ref{sec:results}).
proposals.new: EFE and Planning are bit-identical at $K{=}1$ and within seed-level sampling error at $K{=}2$ ($43.2\%$ against $43.8\%$ success). Evidence of a gap with two tests comes from the main Diagnosis battery of Section~\ref{sec:results}.
proposals.rationale: Separates the parenthetical qualification and states what the cited battery contributes. All values and the cross-reference are preserved.

proposals.old: with each of these panel's titles also reporting
proposals.new: with each panel's title also reporting
proposals.rationale: Corrects a plural possessive construction in the accessibility description.

proposals.old: Information arrives as a side effect of translation, and greedy progress toward the belief mode already provides correlated evidence.
proposals.new: Information arrives as a side effect of movement, and greedy progress toward the belief mode already provides correlated evidence.
proposals.rationale: Uses the ordinary term for the move actions the paragraph has just introduced.

proposals.old: The main-text table (Table~\ref{tab:main}) reports the seed-level SE as the primary uncertainty measure, since each answers a different question (episode-level precision versus between-seed replicability) and neither alone is a strict superset of the other.
proposals.new: The main-text table (Table~\ref{tab:main}) reports the seed-level SE as the primary uncertainty measure. Pooled episode-level and seed-level SE describe different sources of variation, episode-level precision and between-seed replicability, so neither replaces the other.
proposals.rationale: Supplies the missing antecedent of “each” and replaces the awkward set-theoretic “strict superset” metaphor while retaining the distinction between uncertainty summaries.

proposals.old: Following the producing script, an environment agrees when $w{=}1$ is near-optimal at $H{=}1$ and at some deeper horizon, or at neither, which holds for 44 of the 100.
proposals.new: Following the producing script, we classify an environment as agreeing across horizons when $w{=}1$ is near-optimal at $H{=}1$ and at some deeper horizon, or at neither. This holds for 44 of the 100 environments.
proposals.rationale: Makes agreement a classification rather than an action by an environment, and separates the count from the definition.

proposals.old: RS[11,11] is exceptional in a different sense, where every tree-search agent, including Planning at $w{=}0$, converges to the same low-activity policy, discussed in Section~\ref{sec:rocksample}.
proposals.new: On RS[11,11], every tree-search agent, including Planning at $w{=}0$, instead converges to the same low-activity policy, discussed in Section~\ref{sec:rocksample}.
proposals.rationale: Removes the awkward “exceptional in a different sense, where” construction without changing the comparison.

proposals.old: Three departures in the search procedure itself remain, all keyed to fully observable quantities (the belief representation and depth-cap leaf value are separate implementation choices, disclosed and sensitivity-checked below).
proposals.new: The search procedure makes three departures, all keyed to fully observable quantities. The belief representation and depth-cap leaf value are separate implementation choices, disclosed and sensitivity-checked below.
proposals.rationale: Separates the important implementation qualification from the introduction to the three departures.

proposals.old: for the three OTC environments where its belief is small enough to reach near-optimal convergence in reasonable time.
proposals.new: for the three OTC environments whose small state spaces allow near-optimal convergence in reasonable time.
proposals.rationale: Replaces “its belief is small enough,” whose referent and meaning are unclear, with the state-space limitation described by the following sentence.

proposals.old: POMCP comparison config (5{,}000 total episodes across 5 per-run seeds $\{42,\allowbreak 123,\allowbreak 456,\allowbreak 789,\allowbreak 1024\}$ for Tiger/Diagnosis/Bandit and 1{,}000 for Tileworld, matching the main-table protocol on those three environments, and EFE/Planning here are re-run inside the POMCP harness rather than sourced from Table~\ref{tab:main}, which they reproduce exactly).
proposals.new: POMCP comparison (5{,}000 total episodes across 5 per-run seeds $\{42,\allowbreak 123,\allowbreak 456,\allowbreak 789,\allowbreak 1024\}$ for Tiger/Diagnosis/Bandit and 1{,}000 for Tileworld). The protocol matches the main table on the three core environments. EFE and Planning are evaluated inside the POMCP harness and reproduce Table~\ref{tab:main} exactly.
proposals.rationale: Breaks a long parenthesis into three sentences and removes the informal “config,” preserving episode counts, seed list, protocol match, and independent evaluation statement.

proposals.old: Neither switchable component shows a detectable effect. No variant differs from the reported configuration on success or reward on any of the three environments after Holm correction within metric.
proposals.new: Neither switchable component shows a detectable effect on success or reward. No variant differs from the reported configuration on either metric on any of the three environments after Holm correction within metric.
proposals.rationale: Scopes the first sentence to the two outcomes actually tested there, so it does not appear contradicted by the significant observation-count change in the next sentence.

proposals.old: a symbol distinct from the observation cost $c$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:nearopt}.
proposals.new: a quantity distinct from the observation cost $c$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:nearopt}.
proposals.rationale: Both quantities use the same printed symbol c. The intended distinction is between quantities, not symbols.

proposals.old: No reported iterate exceeded $3.1$, more than an order of magnitude below $w_{\max}$, so the upper projection never bound, but it is in force.
proposals.new: No reported iterate exceeded $3.1$, more than an order of magnitude below $w_{\max}$, so the upper bound was never reached, although the projection remained in force.
proposals.rationale: Replaces the awkward verb “bound” with a clear statement of the same observed fact and safeguard.
Uses a natural, precise description of the sample-size motivation without changing the prospective-study disclosure that follows.

proposals.old: The two remaining held-out shortfalls are Diagnosis at $B{=}9.53$ and Bandit's gap budget.
proposals.new: In the predeclared comparison at $B$, the two held-out shortfalls are Diagnosis at $B{=}9.53$ and Bandit's gap budget.
proposals.rationale: The preceding sentence concerns the post hoc realized-usage sensitivity, where the held-out Bandit interval includes zero. Explicitly returns the reader to the predeclared target-at-B comparison without changing its result.

proposals.old: On $N{=}16$, EFE's reward deficit to Planning ($-45.80$ against $-45.42$) is not significant ($p{=}0.57$), so the two reward cells are bolded together, EFE's $+12.6$pp accuracy gain over Planning has $p<10^{-7}$, and Planning+IG ($w{=}5$) runs $38.3 \pm 0.05$ tests against EFE's $28.1 \pm 0.09$ (seed-level SE), roughly $36\%$ more (seed-level Welch $p{=}1.7{\times}10^{-11}$).
proposals.new: On $N{=}16$, EFE's reward deficit to Planning ($-45.80$ against $-45.42$) is not significant ($p{=}0.57$), so the two reward cells are bolded together. EFE's $+12.6$pp accuracy gain over Planning has $p<10^{-7}$. Planning+IG ($w{=}5$) runs $38.3 \pm 0.05$ tests against EFE's $28.1 \pm 0.09$ (seed-level SE), roughly $36\%$ more (seed-level Welch $p{=}1.7{\times}10^{-11}$).
proposals.rationale: Separates reward, accuracy, and sensing-count results into readable sentences, preserving every numerical value and statistical qualifier.

proposals.old: Effect sizes clarify where the differences lie, read on the conventional bands that Table~\ref{tab:effect_sizes} lists.
proposals.new: Effect sizes clarify where the differences lie, using the conventional interpretation bands listed in Table~\ref{tab:effect_sizes}.
proposals.rationale: Removes the dangling and unnatural “read on” construction.

experiments/run_nearopt_horizon.py:97–98 computes threshold = max(0.05 * abs(best_reward), 0.5) and near_opt = gap <= threshold.
